title: pm-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-11
content:
Morning brain dump / running list - 2026-03-11

Context: final prep for hosted API embedding feature launch (soft launch to beta orgs next week). Working through PRD edits, rollout plan, and outstanding asks from infra and SRE. Mostly scratch notes - prioritizing what I need to unblock today.

Top priorities (today)
- Finish PRD edits: remove ambiguous acceptance criteria on 'embedding freshness' and add explicit SLOs for inference latency (p50/p95) + sync with SRE.
- Confirm canary rollout plan with infra + seeding orgs (Ben) - timeline + rollback triggers.
- Finalize telemetry dashboards and alert thresholds (Maya) - need list of key metrics to check during canary.
- Draft customer comms + internal ops runbook for beta (short, clear steps).

Meetings
- 09:00 sync w/infra (Ben) - confirm canary nodes, capacity reservation, autoscale policy for initial traffic.
- 10:30 SRE triage - failure mode discussion + rollback thresholds.
- 13:00 PM sync (product) - go/no-go checklist review.
- 15:00 Legal quick call about data residency note for a partner.

PRD edits (inline TODOs)
- Rewrite Acceptance Criteria #2: currently says "reasonable latency" -> change to "inference p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms for typical 512-token embeddings on g5.xlarge".
- Add a non-functional requirement: "Embedding vectors must be stable across minor model patch releases unless otherwise specified; breaking changes require migration notes and vector reindexing guidance."
- Section: "Backwards compatibility": add guidance for model variants and recommended migration path (small code snippet + example).
- Add "Canary success signals" subsection with concrete metrics: error rate < 0.5% sustained for 10m, 95th latency within baseline + 20%, no spike in token-level cost beyond 10%.

Rollout / Canary plan (high level)
- Phase 0: internal smoke test on staging + core infra runbook exercise (today).
- Phase 1: 2 beta orgs, 5% of traffic, 24h monitoring window.
- Phase 2: 25% traffic if Phase 1 ok, 72h window, ramp policy.
- Rollback triggers: sustained error rate > 1% for 5m OR p95 latency > 3x baseline for 5m OR data residency violation.
- Manual aborters: product lead (me), infra lead (Ben), SRE on-call.

Telemetry & dashboards (Maya) - needs
- Per-org success rate + error breakdown (client error vs infra).
- Latency histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99) by model + region.
- Cost per 1k tokens / embeddings.
- KV cache hit rate + cache fill metrics.
- Alerting: paged if error rate anomalies or p95 beyond threshold.

Outstanding blockers
- infra: confirm persistent KV cache will be available in canary (Ben said investigating - follow up after 09:00).
- SRE: need a pre-written runbook page with exact playbook for rollback (Maya to draft, due EOD).
- Legal: short data residency blurb for partner onboarding (call 15:00).
- SDK: small API change? Confirm whether we need to bump client minor version for structured output flag (Ethan to confirm).

Customer comms (draft bullets)
- Beta launch next Tue; invited orgs will see a new endpoint /v1/embeddings-beta.
- Note: vector stability guaranteed across minor infra patches; major model upgrades may require reindexing - we will provide migration tooling.
- If you have data residency constraints, contact your CSM; see linked doc.

Quick TODOs (one-line)
- [ ] Update PRD acceptance criteria (finish w/ examples) - due EOD.
- [ ] Post canary plan to #product-launch channel after infra sync.
- [ ] Ask infra for exact instance types + estimated token throughput for initial canary.
- [ ] Confirm with SDK team re: structured-output flag behavior.
- [ ] Draft runbook skeleton in Confluence and link here.
- [ ] Prep quick internal demo for Beta orgs (2 short prompts + expected outputs).

Notes to self (random)
- Keep launch comms short and explicit; ops runbook needs exact commands (no ambiguous steps).
- When writing the PRD, use numbers and concrete thresholds wherever possible - avoids long Slack threads.
- Remember to capture post-canary evaluation criteria (quality regression checks tied to eval prompt set).

Decisions made earlier
- Use 5% initial traffic canary instead of 1% because infra wanted meaningful load to test autoscale.
- Keep default model variant conservative (quantized medium) for cost control, offer high-precision variant opt-in.

Unresolved questions
- Do we need an explicit SLA note for beta customers? (legal/input: probably not, but need to make expectations clear).
- SDK change: breaking? check PR #2143 (linked).

End-of-day goals
- PRD edits merged + comment addressing all reviewer feedback.
- Canary plan posted + infra confirmation.
- Runbook skeleton in Confluence with assigned owners.

Random scratch: potential follow-up items for next week
- Post-canary retrospective template (metrics we'll collect).
- Automated canary analysis job to surface regressions in prompt-level evals.
- Cost guardrails to prevent unexpected spend during ramp.

---
If anything comes up during morning calls, jot here and move to PRD or runbook as needed.
